sources.note: Uses chain-of-thought about required capabilities as training-time supervision for a skill retriever -- distilled from a teacher in stage one and refined by retrieval-rewarded GRPO in stage two -- so that at inference the model encodes the bare query with no generation at all.
sources.title: SkillReason: Reasoning-Enhanced Agent Skill Retrieval for Implicit User Requests

sources.note: Probes and steers across the trunk-to-diffusion boundary of an AlphaFold3-class structure predictor, finding that geometry survives the crossing while sequence chemistry is attenuated, and that a strand direction predictive at F1 0.82 steers nothing at all -- with an architectural explanation for why.
sources.title: Probing and steering biology across Boltz-1s trunk-diffusion boundary

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'annotation incompleteness'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. The wiki already links entities that turn up in the same summary; what it cannot see is the neighbour a reader would actually want next — the generation before this one, the benchmark it was built to beat, the method it replaces. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:
- Write in en.
- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.
- No marketing language. Prefer the specific number over the adjective.
- Return one JSON object matching the schema exactly. No prose around it.

result.definition: When the reference labels cover only part of what is actually present, so a model that is right about an unlabelled case is scored as wrong. Both sources treat it as a measurement problem to be quantified rather than a caveat to be mentioned. The protein-probing work supplies the cleanest demonstration: identical activations decode the same concept at F1 0.85 against dense structural labels and 0.42 against sparse experimental annotations, and a self-consistency check that recomputes the dense labels on the model's own predicted structure moves the score by only 0.06 to 0.08 -- ruling out structural disagreement and establishing the gap as missing labels, so every score against the sparse set is a lower bound. The skill-retrieval work addresses the same problem on the evaluation side, where a benchmark assigns one official target per query although a large corpus may hold several functionally substitutable answers; it responds with a sensitivity analysis crediting independently reviewed alternatives, which moves every retriever by a comparable margin (+1.37 to +3.54 Recall@1) and leaves the ordering intact. Together the sources give both the diagnosis and the two available responses -- measure the gap against a denser label set, or measure how much crediting the missing positives would move the ranking -- and the shared conclusion is that cross-paper comparisons are only meaningful at matched label density.
